title: SDK Stability Matrix, Downgrade Guarantees, and Acceptance Criteria for Pagination/Retry/Streaming
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Purpose: Define a clear, testable PRD that codifies compatibility guarantees across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs for pagination, retries, and streaming APIs. Deliverables: compatibility matrix by language and SDK minor/major version, explicit downgrade and graceful-degradation semantics, concrete acceptance criteria and automated tests, documentation and migration notes for customers, and a rollout plan that minimizes runtime regressions. This PRD captures scope, non-goals, trade-offs, and acceptance tests for the Q2 SDK stability initiative.
scope: In-scope: public client surface for generation, streaming chat, list/paginated endpoints (embeddings, logs), client-side retry semantics, on-wire streaming formats, and language-specific behavior exceptions. Out-of-scope: server-side runtime kernel changes, internal routing fallbacks, and third-party SDK wrappers maintained by partners.
requirements: Compatibility matrix: define compatibility tiers (Guaranteed, Best-effort, Advisory) per language for minor and patch releases

Downgrade guarantees: apps using older client minor versions must continue to work with new server releases for at least two server major/minor cycles unless opt-in breaking change is announced 30 days in advance
Pagination contract: standardized cursor token format (opaque string), page_size semantics, stable ordering guarantee for list endpoints used by SDK iterators
Streaming contract: explicit chunk envelope with event-type metadata, client-side resumable checkpoint token for long-lived streams, backpressure guidance for buffered consumers
Retry policy: default idempotency classification per API, recommended backoff parameters, SDK helper utilities to wrap non-idempotent operations with safe retries
Language exceptions: document and test behavior divergences for Python asyncio, Node.js native streams, and Go channel/ctx semantics
Docs and migration guides: per-language upgrade doc with code samples and a 'how to roll back' checklist
Automated tests: unit and integration tests that run against server release candidates validating pagination cursors, streaming resume, and retry observability
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix published in the SDK docs and linked from changelog
End-to-end test harness validates streaming resume for payloads >= 5MB in all three languages
Iterator/pagination helpers return deterministic ordering in 99.9% of runs under load (latency and concurrency fuzzing integrated into tests)
Default retry helpers align with platform telemetry (same number of retries and backoff at P95) and expose configuration knobs
Degradation behavior defined: when a newer server disables a feature, SDKs will emit a typed warning and fall back to best-effort behavior without throwing by default
Release notes include explicit migration steps and a compatibility flag that teams can set to opt into stricter behavior
API surface changes gated behind feature flags for 2 release cycles and feature-flag tests added to CI matrix
acceptance_test_plan: 1) Add integration job in CI that runs a matrix of Python/TS/Go against SDK release candidate and a server RC. 2) Create synthetic workload that streams 100 concurrent user sessions with interleaved pagination queries and intentionally induced transient failures. 3) Assert on resume correctness, cursor monotonicity, and retry counts. 4) Run mutation tests where SDK uses older minor version against server RC to validate downgrade guarantees.
milestones: Draft PRD and review with eng/design - 2026-03-05
Align on compatibility tiers and publish matrix - 2026-03-12
open_questions: What is the canonical on-wire streaming framing format we commit to for 2 years? (chunked NDJSON vs SSE with typed events)
Should resumable stream tokens be first-class objects in SDKs or opaque strings returned from the server?
How do we handle ordering guarantees for paginated endpoints where backend ownership spans multiple services?
Is 30 days sufficient notice for breaking changes that affect client iterators used in background jobs?
decisions: Prefer opaque resume tokens returned by server; SDKs provide helpers to capture/restore them
Expose a single 'streamingMode' opt-in in SDKs: 'strict' (throws on missing fields) and 'lenient' (best-effort fallback), default 'lenient' for major/patch compat
Pagination cursors are considered opaque; SDKs will never parse cursor contents but will validate length/pattern to detect corruption
Retry helpers default to exponential backoff with jitter and a max of 4 retries for idempotent calls; non-idempotent helpers must be explicit
review_history: 2026-03-01: PM review w/ Eng (Kira Morales) - requested stronger downgrade guarantee wording
2026-03-02: Design review (Ethan Martinez) - recommended streamingMode flag UX and sample snippets
2026-03-04: Security (Avery Li) - no cryptographic changes required; recommend threat model doc for resume tokens
notes: Trade-offs: strict guarantees increase server testing surface and slow down rollout; default lenient mode reduces customer impact but requires better telemetry
We should track number of clients using 'strict' mode and failures post-release to decide whether to flip default after 2 quarters
Consider adding an automated migration runner that tests a customer's code path against new server RCs for high-value customers
follow_ups: Create RFC for streaming framing format if stakeholders can't converge by 2026-03-09
Add telemetry hooks to identify SDKs that invoke retry helpers with custom settings
Schedule compatibility review gate for runtime-1.22 release to validate this PRD's guarantees
